plan.summary: How to set up and keep a disciplined developer workstation: shell, git, editor, AI-assisted coding, and Node version management, so every later frontend topic starts from a reproducible base.
outcomes: Explain why a disciplined, reproducible workstation pays off every day.
Explain what PATH and environment variables do when a command runs.
Build a dotfiles repository that reproduces your setup on a new machine.
Decide between merge and rebase for a given branch history.
Decide how to use an AI coding agent without trusting its output.
Build a git bisect run that finds the commit that introduced a bug.

lesson_outline.title: Why your workstation matters
lesson_outline.visual_reason: A concrete story of a slow, unreproducible setup is enough to show the cost.

lesson_outline.title: Terminal & shell fluency
lesson_outline.visual_reason: A pipe that filters and transforms text is read line by line.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Step through a pipeline and predict what each stage passes on.

lesson_outline.title: Git & GitHub fluency
lesson_outline.visual_reason: A branch-and-merge workflow is a graph, best drawn once and reused.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Order the git commands for a feature branch and predict the history.

lesson_outline.title: Your editor, sharpened
lesson_outline.visual_reason: A small map of editor features and their shortcuts is all this idea needs.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Match each editor feature to the shortcut or command that invokes it.

lesson_outline.title: AI-assisted development, done safely
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Prompt, review, test, and merge form one review loop; a workflow view fits.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Sort each AI output into the review action it needs before merge.

video.reason: Prompt, generate, test, and merge form a chronological loop that motion explains better than a picture.

lesson_outline.title: Node.js & version management
lesson_outline.visual_reason: One runtime with several installed versions is a small static structure.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Match each Node tool (node, npx, a version manager) to what it does.

lesson_outline.title: A production team's setup
lesson_outline.visual_reason: A team standardizes workstation, CI, and version policy; a workflow diagram ties it together.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Choose the workstation change a team should make given a symptom.

mini_projects.use_case: A developer reproduces their whole shell, git, and editor setup on a new machine from one repository and an install script.
A developer uses git bisect to find the exact commit that introduced a bug in a small demo repository.

capstone.name: Dev environment configurator
capstone.problem: A developer picks their shell, git identity, editor, and Node version in a web form and receives a ready dotfiles repository with an install script and a setup checklist, with tests.

learner.experience: software developer learning frontend end to end

curriculum.scope: Set up and keep a disciplined developer workstation: shell, git, editor, AI-assisted coding, and Node version management, as the reproducible base for every later frontend topic.

discovery.note: Sub-concepts proposed by discovery (pipes-and-redirection, path-and-environment-variables, signals-and-job-control, dotfiles-and-shell-config, git-identity-and-auth, commit-graph-and-branches, merge-strategy, git-bisect, pr-review-workflow) are folded into their parent concepts at standard depth; merge-strategy and git-bisect evidence is covered by pro-git-book. editor-setup and node-version-management were investigated by the docs and repos category units. The macOS shell-default claim in the MIT lecture was not independently confirmed and is not cited in teaching material.
